# Query Selector

The `document.querySelector()` method finds the first element on the page that matches a CSS selector. Use it when your JavaScript needs to select an element by class, `id`, tag name, or another selector.
examples: [{"name":"Select an Element by Class","description":"This selects the first element with the class `bell-icon.`","code":"`const bellIcon = document.querySelector(\".bell-icon\");`"}]
name: Query Selector
tips:
- `document.querySelector()` selects the first element that matches the selector.
- Use `.` before a class name, like `".bell-icon"`.
- Use `#` before an `id`, like `"#message"`.
- Remember to put the selector inside quotation marks.
- In Web Lab, this method often appears near the top of `script.js` to store page elements in variables.
